name: Ulysses
kicker: Joyce’s modernist novel · One Dublin day echoing Homer’s Odyssey
briefing: On June 16, 1904, an ordinary Dublin ad salesman named Leopold Bloom wanders the city buying soap, attending a funeral, and quietly worrying about his wife Molly’s afternoon visitor. James Joyce turned that single ordinary day into one of the most ambitious novels ever written, loosely retelling Homer’s _Odyssey_ scene by scene. _Ulysses_ made the stream of consciousness style famous, pouring its characters’ raw thoughts straight onto the page, and fans still celebrate June 16 every year as “Bloomsday.”

qb.tip: Zero hits at Middle School/Easy High School — this novel is mainly a Regular HS/College topic. Searching “Ulysses” without a category filter also pulls in Tennyson’s poem of that name and the mythological Odysseus (sometimes accepted as “Ulysses”); those are a different answer line and were skipped.

sample.note: 4 real QBReader tossups (0 Middle School/Easy High School + 4 Regular High School, power-marked); a few additional “Ulysses” hits were really about the mythological Odysseus or Tennyson’s poem and were not counted.

tossups.p: This novel opens with the line “Stately, plump Buck Mulligan came from the stairhead, bearing a bowl of lather.” That same morning, Mulligan argues with his gloomy roommate, a young teacher and poet named Stephen Dedalus.
tossups.r: Elsewhere in Dublin, an advertising canvasser named Leopold Bloom spends the day attending a funeral, eating a kidney for breakfast, and worrying about his wife’s plans to meet another man. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel set on a single day in 1904.

tossups.p: One character in this novel tells his employer that “history is a nightmare from which I am trying to awake” during a conversation in which that headmaster makes antisemitic remarks. That character, Stephen Dedalus, is still mourning his mother’s recent death.
tossups.r: Meanwhile, Leopold Bloom wanders Dublin thinking about his wife Molly’s afternoon visitor, Blazes Boylan. The novel ends with Molly’s long unpunctuated monologue, which repeats the word “yes.” For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel set on June 16, 1904.

tossups.p: This novel’s protagonist writes to a woman named Martha Clifford under the pen name Henry Flower. That protagonist, Leopold Bloom, picks up her reply at the post office before continuing his errands around Dublin.
tossups.r: Bloom spends the day avoiding his house, since he knows his wife Molly is expecting a visit from Blazes Boylan. The novel’s final chapter is Molly’s famous soliloquy, ending with the word “yes.” For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel narrating a single day in Dublin.

tossups.p: In one chapter of this novel, a fiercely nationalist character called the Citizen argues with the protagonist at Barney Kiernan’s pub and hurls a biscuit tin at him as he leaves. That chapter’s exaggerated, mock-heroic style parodies old Irish legends.
tossups.r: The protagonist of this novel, Leopold Bloom, faces prejudice because he is Jewish throughout the book. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel that also follows the young writer Stephen Dedalus through Dublin on a single day.

tossups.p: A chapter of this novel set on Sandymount Strand follows the protagonist’s thoughts as he watches a young woman named Gerty MacDowell on the beach. That chapter imitates the sentimental style of romance novels.
tossups.r: The protagonist, advertising canvasser Leopold Bloom, spends the day avoiding home, since his wife Molly is expecting Blazes Boylan. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel set in Dublin on June 16, 1904.

tossups.p: One chapter of this novel is broken up with newspaper-style headlines as its characters debate rhetoric inside a Dublin newspaper office. Another chapter mimics the historical development of English prose style across centuries.
tossups.r: The novel as a whole loosely retells Homer’s _Odyssey_, with ad canvasser Leopold Bloom standing in for the wandering hero and his wife Molly standing in for the faithful Penelope. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel.

tossups.p: A 1933 court ruling by judge John Woolsey lifted a long obscenity ban on this novel in the United States, after an earlier magazine serialization had led to a similar court case. It had first been published in full in Paris in 1922 by Sylvia Beach’s bookshop, Shakespeare and Company.
tossups.r: The novel follows Leopold Bloom and the young writer Stephen Dedalus through Dublin on a single day, echoing Homer’s _Odyssey_. For 10 points, name this stream-of-consciousness novel by James Joyce.

tossups.p: Fans of this novel celebrate its setting every year on June 16, a holiday nicknamed after one of its characters. Celebrants often eat the same lunch its protagonist does, a Gorgonzola cheese sandwich at a Dublin pub called Davy Byrne’s.
tossups.r: That protagonist, Leopold Bloom, spends the day avoiding home while his wife Molly expects a visit from Blazes Boylan. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel, whose title alludes to Homer’s wandering hero.

tossups.p: This novel’s final chapter is a long, nearly unpunctuated monologue spoken by a woman recalling her husband’s marriage proposal and ending with the word “yes” repeated several times. That woman, Molly Bloom, has spent the afternoon with her lover Blazes Boylan.
tossups.r: Molly’s husband, Leopold Bloom, spends the novel wandering Dublin while young writer Stephen Dedalus deals with his own troubles. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel set on a single day in 1904.

tossups.p: Throughout this novel, its protagonist grows increasingly anxious about his wife’s planned afternoon meeting with a boastful concert promoter named Blazes Boylan. He distracts himself with errands, a funeral, and a stop at a pub for lunch.
tossups.r: That protagonist, Leopold Bloom, shares the spotlight with young writer Stephen Dedalus, who begins the novel arguing with his roommate Buck Mulligan. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel set in Dublin on a single day in June 1904.

tossups.p: One character in this novel scribbles a short poem on a scrap torn from the headmaster Mr. Deasy’s letter about cattle disease. That character, Stephen Dedalus, had promised to help get Deasy’s letter printed in a newspaper.
tossups.r: Meanwhile, a man named Bantam Lyons mistakes something Leopold Bloom says about a newspaper for a hot tip on a horse race. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel following Stephen and Bloom through Dublin on a single day.

tossups.p: In one scene of this novel, a character notices the letters “I.N.R.I.” or “I.H.S.” embroidered on the back of a priest’s vestments and wonders what they mean. That same character later visits the Freeman’s Journal office to arrange an advertisement for a merchant named Keyes.
tossups.r: This novel’s protagonist, Leopold Bloom, spends the day thinking about his wife Molly’s afternoon visitor, Blazes Boylan. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel that ends with Molly’s soliloquy.

tossups.p: Though the published text does not print them, this novel’s eighteen chapters are traditionally nicknamed after episodes of Homer’s _Odyssey_, such as “Calypso,” “Nausicaa,” and “Penelope.” Critics use these nicknames to describe the novel’s shifting styles, which range from newspaper headlines to a play script.
tossups.r: The novel’s Odysseus figure, Leopold Bloom, wanders Dublin on a single day while his wife Molly, standing in for Penelope, waits at home. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel.

tossups.p: This novel’s protagonist is a Jewish Dubliner who faces casual antisemitism from several characters over the course of a single day, including an argument at a pub that ends with a thrown biscuit tin. He is also haunted by the death of his infant son, Rudy, years earlier.
tossups.r: That protagonist, advertising canvasser Leopold Bloom, shares the novel with a young writer named Stephen Dedalus. For 10 points, name this James Joyce novel that ends with wife Molly Bloom’s famous soliloquy.

tossups.p: This novel famously pours characters’ raw, often unpunctuated thoughts directly onto the page, as in Stephen Dedalus’s musings on Sandymount Strand and its closing chapter narrated by Molly Bloom. T. S. Eliot called it one of the most important books of its era.
tossups.r: Leopold Bloom, the novel’s Odysseus-like hero, spends the day wandering Dublin while Molly awaits a visit from Blazes Boylan. For 10 points, name this stream-of-consciousness novel by James Joyce.

trap.title: Which “Ulysses”?
trap.body: Three different things share this title: Homer’s Greek hero Odysseus (whose Latin name is Ulysses), Alfred, Lord Tennyson’s 1833 poem about that hero’s old age (“To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield”), and James Joyce’s 1922 novel. Clues about Troy, the Cyclops, Penelope, or Ithaca usually point to the mythological hero or Tennyson’s poem, not this novel. Also watch out for Ulysses S. Grant, the Civil War general and U.S. president.
trap.fix: Wait for clues naming Leopold Bloom, Molly, Stephen Dedalus, Dublin, or June 16, 1904 — those confirm the answer is Joyce’s novel, not the myth, the poem, or the president.
trap.line: Real answer line: Ulysses (reject Odysseus and Ulysses S. Grant).
